issue.title: test_ace_page_fast_startup_is_structurally_quiet fails under the full parallel lane: a Textual worker is still unfinished after AcePage exits
issue.description:
REPRODUCTION: tests/test_ace_testing.py::test_ace_page_fast_startup_is_structurally_quiet failed once under the full parallel lane during a monitored 'just check-full' at HEAD 423669549 (monitor j529c27q5gye, 2026-08-17): '1 failed, 32563 passed, 13 skipped, 70 warnings in 1144.43s'. It was the ONLY failing node in the run, and its failure is what turned 'just test-cost' (Justfile:401) and therefore check-full red.

EXACT FAILURE (tests/test_ace_testing.py:169, the post-exit block after the 'async with AcePage() as page' body):
    assert all(worker.is_finished for worker in app.workers)
    E       assert False
    E        +  where False = all(<generator object ...<genexpr>>)
Every earlier assertion in that test passed, including the in-context structural-quiet assertions and the three post-exit assertions above it (_fs_watcher/_prompt_source_watcher/_stall_watchdog are None, _pump_free_async_tasks empty). So the app tore down its watchers and timers correctly and only a Textual worker was still unfinished when the context manager returned.

NOT REPRODUCED under narrower lanes (this is the useful negative evidence for whoever picks this up):
  - alone: 1 passed
  - whole module, default lane, 5 consecutive runs: 35 passed each time
  - whole module co-run with the bead/chop tests that landed alongside it: 94 passed
  - 'just test-contention -- tests/test_ace_testing.py' (the instrument sase-ct's retirement policy names): 'contention tally: 0 node(s) failed across 3 repeat(s) in 225.7s; red repeats: none'
That last one matters: pinned-CPU starvation restricted to this file does NOT reproduce it, so the trigger is very likely cross-FILE interaction in the whole-suite lane rather than intra-file load. A fix attempt that only soaks this file will look green while proving nothing.

NOT A PROCESS-GLOBAL-STATE LEAK, at least not one the current detector sees: the same failing run's sase global leak detector reported '0 poisoning change(s) across 0 test(s); 30980 warming mutation(s) filtered; 302 cooling mutation(s) filtered; 1122 invalidation(s) filtered'. So this is a worker/task lifecycle race, distinct in mechanism from the config/registry state-leak nodes that dominate this flake class.

STATUS: this node is NOT in tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt and 'grep' over the durable flake-evidence store found no prior failure record for it, so 2026-08-17 is its first recorded sighting.

SCOPE: determine which Textual worker is still running when AcePage.__aexit__ returns under the full lane, then either make the harness await/cancel it deterministically before the assertion or fix the production path that leaves it outstanding. Prefer a mechanism fix over baselining the node; if it has to be baselined first, the baseline entry needs this bead named as owner per the header of tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt.

PROPOSED BY: the land agent for epic sase-on, which is NOT the cause: that epic's six commits touch zero src/sase/ace/** files and zero ACE tests (they touch bead config/triage/stale-cleanup, notification gate wiring, default_config.yml, sase.schema.json and docs), and the co-run above rules out its new tests interfering.

evidence.note: Independently reproduced 2026-08-18 under just test-scoped after it escalated to the full parallel lane (14 workers, 33820 items) while implementing kill_and_edit_explicit_id. Failure: leftover cancelled pump-free task sase-artifacts-project-choices after AcePage exit (assert not app._pump_free_async_tasks). Serial rerun of tests/test_ace_testing.py::test_ace_page_fast_startup_is_structurally_quiet on the same tree passed in 1.81s. Unrelated to the kill-and-edit diff: no ACE page/startup code was touched.

Independent reproduction on master ec048b168 + a local tests/_suite_gate.py module split (test-support refactor only; zero src/sase changes and zero ACE/TUI files touched). Two consecutive 'just check' runs in workspace sase_15 on 2026-08-18 escalated to the full lane (root-conftest broadening rule) and this node failed in both: run 1 '2 failed, 33801 passed, 13 skipped, 45 errors in 529.94s', run 2 '2 failed, 33801 passed, 13 skipped in 550.51s'. Rerunning the node serially on the identical tree passed in 1.05s.

NEW SIGNATURE, one assertion EARLIER than the one this bead documents. Run 2 failed at tests/test_ace_testing.py:168 on 'assert not app._pump_free_async_tasks', with a leftover CANCELLED task: {<Task cancelled name='sase-artifacts-project-choices' coro=<ArtifactsMixin._ensure_artifacts_project_choices.<locals>... defined at src/sase/ace/tui/actions/artifacts.py:314>>}. This bead's description explicitly records _pump_free_async_tasks as EMPTY in the original sighting, with only line 169's 'all(worker.is_finished ...)' failing. So the AcePage teardown race leaves at least two distinct kinds of outstanding background work behind, not just Textual workers: whoever fixes this should treat _ensure_artifacts_project_choices' pump-free task as a second reproduction path and check whether one mechanism (deterministic await/cancel-and-drain in AcePage.__aexit__) covers both, rather than fixing only the worker assertion.

Independent reproduction on 2026-08-18 while implementing the Current Project glossary term (sase.yml + generated instruction files only; no ACE/TUI or current-project code touched). just check scoped lane in workspace sase_13 escalated to a 33832-item parallel run: tests/test_ace_testing.py::test_ace_page_fast_startup_is_structurally_quiet failed at tests/test_ace_testing.py:168 with leftover cancelled pump-free task sase-artifacts-project-choices from ArtifactsMixin._ensure_artifacts_project_choices (artifacts.py:314). Same new signature already recorded by 074: assert not app._pump_free_async_tasks, not the original unfinished-worker assertion. Serial rerun of this node together with the other failing node on the identical tree passed in 2.13s (1.13s for this node). Parallel-only; ran on gw4. Suite result: 2 failed, 33830 passed, 13 skipped in 538.48s.

Independent reproduction from a third epic and a different host tree: phase bead sase-pv.8 (epic sase-pv, "A feature flag is a task bead, not a bead type") recorded test_ace_page_fast_startup_is_structurally_quiet failing once under its escalated full-suite run on 2026-08-19T00:14:49Z and passing on a serial rerun of the same tree. Its stated signature matches this bead: a leftover cancelled "sase-artifacts-project-choices" task still outstanding after AcePage exits.

Reached from a diff that touched no ACE, Textual, or artifact code at all -- sase-pv.8 deleted the `flag` bead issue type from the Rust wire, the Python model, the storage codecs, and the compatibility mirror. That is the third unrelated epic (after sase-on and sase-p8) to hit this node incidentally, which further supports this bead's "load-dependent, not diff-dependent" reading.

New detail this report adds: the leftover work is NAMED. Previous evidence said only "a Textual worker is still unfinished"; sase-pv.8 identified it as a cancelled sase-artifacts-project-choices task surviving AcePage teardown. That is a concrete starting point -- whoever works this should check whether cancellation of that specific task is awaited before the AcePage context manager returns.
